question: do the two near-breakeven effects - a rare origin and a trending return - stack on the nested one (a 15m/30m zone inside a 4h break's leg) to cross zero?

rules.S1: S0 and er_r >= its 60th percentile (Kaufman efficiency, 10 bars, before the return)
rules.S2: S0 and stretch >= its 80th percentile (the 50-bar EMA minus the origin low, ATR)

thresholds: percentiles of all qualified 15m/30m first returns in the MT5 run (discovery), per timeframe, computed mechanically - no other choice made after seeing results
judged_once_on: Binance perpetuals, 12 coins, 15m and 30m, 2021-01 to 2024-06 and 2024-07 on, fees 0.07%
passes_if: R a trade > 0 on Binance 30m in both periods, and the day-bootstrap 90% interval of R over the whole Binance sample above 0
result: as first run: S2 passed on Binance 30m (+0.177R) and S3 (+0.112R) - but the 'inside' flag used 4h breaks not yet known at the entry. Causal (4h break known before entry): S1 -0.127, S2 -0.045 [-0.101, +0.013], S3 -0.037 on Binance 30m: all fail. VOID as a pass.
